To preface: A checkpoint is a subcategory of challenge, so every
checkpoint is a challenge, but sprints and races can also be challenges.

Some of the following documentation includes features that are
implemented for all types of challenges, but it is aimed at introducing
the new features of the checkpoints.

# ![](data:image/png;base64,){width="2.6462292213473315in" height="2.6331944444444444in"}Create a checkpoint

This is in the "Developing" stage of a field of studies where it is
possible to create Challenges (i.e. Races, Sprints and/or Checkpoints)

To get to the overview of created challenges, click the Item
"Challenges" on the left sidebar.

To create a checkpoint, click the "create challenge" button, to then
select "Checkpoint". This leads to the following creation pages, with a
general tab and a questions tab

## General Tab![](data:image/png;base64,){width="3.215239501312336in" height="4.565076552930884in"}

The general tab is the place to determine any metadata about the
Checkpoint

### Name

The title of the checkpoint as it will show up both to educators and
students.

Its length is limited to 20 characters

### Description

The description of the checkpoint will also show up both to educators
and students. The buttons above allow for formatting

### Dependency

Can be set to either "Chain", "Time", or "Chain&Time".

Chain dependency makes it possible to select challenges of any type in
the right side bar which are to be completed before the start of the
current
checkpoint.![](data:image/png;base64,){width="2.7031255468066493in"
height="0.47304680664916887in"}

Time dependency makes it possible and necessary to select the earliest
possible and the latest possible start date.

### Duration

It is measured in minutes. After a student starts the checkpoint, the
student has *duration* amount of time to complete it. When the time is
over, it is automatically submitted.

The duration has to be at least 1 and at most 200.

### Subjects

This field works as before.

### Deleting the checkpoint

On the bottom, there is the possibility to delete the challenge. This is
not reversible, which is why you are prompted to confirm when pressing
this button. Deleting a checkpoint also deletes the associated question
files.

## Questions Tab

### Navigation

When navigating the existing questions, it is possible to delete
questions (and variants) via the trash icon, and it is also possible to
display the whole question text and answer possibilities by clicking on
the respective fields.

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="5.413443788276465in"
height="4.505208880139983in"}

### Sections

#### Add section![](data:image/png;base64,){width="3.7988298337707787in" height="2.5052088801399823in"}

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="1.1927088801399826in"
height="0.3527734033245844in"}

Pressing this button adds a section

After adding the title (and optionally the description), press the "Add
section" button again.

#### Section Title

Title of the section as it is shown to students

#### Section Description

Description of the section as it is shown to
students![](data:image/png;base64,){width="3.8020833333333335in"
height="1.7494641294838145in"}

#### Shuffle Sections

A toggle button that decides whether or not sections are to be shuffled.
If they are shuffled, each student gets the order of the sections
assigned randomly

#### Delete Section

This deletes a section from the checkpoint

#### Shuffle Questions

Toggle button that decides whether or not the questions inside a section
are to be shuffled.

### Questions![](data:image/png;base64,){width="1.3177088801399826in" height="0.26190507436570426in"}

To add a new question inside a section, press the "Add New Question"
button.

There are some fields that are common to each question type:

Question Text: The question as it is shown to the student

Max Marks: The maximum mark a student can reach with this question

Explanation: An explanation as to why the correct answer is the correct
answer. This only shows up to students when they review their checkpoint
after it has been graded

Question Media: Pressing this field prompts the user to upload images
which will show up to the students for that specific question.

After having filled in all necessary fields, press the "Add question"
button to add the question to the section.

#### Open-ended

Additionally to the common fields, the open-ended question type has a
text field for the correct answer. This, along with the question text
and explanation is used in the automatic grading by AI.

#### Single choice![](data:image/png;base64,){width="3.3593755468066493in" height="1.540178258967629in"}

Add option: To add an option, type the option into the text field and
press the "Add option" button. The option then shows up above it, along
with the option to delete it.

Choose the correct answer: This allows to choose which of the given
options is
correct![](data:image/png;base64,){width="5.421875546806649in"
height="1.4860618985126859in"}

#### Multiple Choice

Add option: Works exactly as in the single choice questions

Choose the correct answer: As opposed to the single choice questions,
the options here are checkboxes, where the user can choose as many as
they like

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="5.026042213473316in"
height="1.2272889326334209in"}

#### Drag&Drop

Question Text: For this question type, the Question Text field changes
to allow for adding blanks. They can be added manually ("{{ }}") or
through a button "Add blank" which adds "{{\_\_}}" to the question text.
The inside of the brackets need to be edited to display the needed
correct text.

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="5.057292213473316in"
height="1.9766174540682415in"}

Add incorrect option: The mechanism is the same as for the single and
multiple choice questions. These options will be displayed as a part of
the answer possibilities to the student

### Variants

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="5.123141951006124in"
height="1.8674278215223097in"}

Adding a variant works just like adding a question, except that you
don't need to specify the max marks as it is the same for each variant
of a question. For each student, one of the variants is selected
randomly for that question.

# Evaluation Page:

The evaluation page displays a list of all students who have completed
the checkpoint. It provides statistics and filtering options to easily
analyze progress. Each entry in the list includes:

-   **Student Name**

-   **Checkpoint Status** (e.g., completed, in progress)

-   **Mentor Mark**

-   **"More" Button** -- Clicking this button opens the detailed view of
    > the student's solved checkpoint.

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="2.125in"}

**Statuses:**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Name**        **Description**
  --------------- -------------------------------------------------------
  In Progress     The checkpoint or evaluation is still being worked on
                  and is not yet ready for grading.

  Ready for       The student has submitted their answers. The submission
  Grading         is locked and is now awaiting grading by a teacher.

  Awaiting        The teacher has graded the submission. The result is
  Student Review  available, but the student has not yet acknowledged or
                  reviewed the feedback.

  Student Review  The student has seen and acknowledged the feedback
  Received        provided by the teacher.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Workflow:

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,){width="5.53125in"
height="7.302083333333333in"}

# Filtering:

Filtering functionality allows teachers to narrow down the list of
checkpoints based on student name or status:

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="4.708333333333333in"
height="0.8645833333333334in"}

-   **Search Bar**:\
    > Teachers can type in a student\'s name to filter and only show
    > relevant checkpoints. The filter is applied in real-time as the
    > name is typed.

-   **Checkpoint Status Dropdown**:\
    > Teachers can select a specific status (e.g., \"In Progress\",
    > \"Ready for Grading\", \"Completed\") from a dropdown menu to
    > filter checkpoints accordingly.\
    > ![](data:image/png;base64,){width="3.21875in"
    > height="2.6979166666666665in"}

Both filters can be used together to precisely find a specific
student\'s checkpoint in a specific status

# Statistics:

At the top of the page, an overview of the checkpoint statistics is
displayed to give the teacher a quick summary:

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="0.3333333333333333in"}

-   **Average Grade**: Mean score across all completed checkpoints.

-   **Median Grade**: Middle value of all grades to reflect performance
    > distribution.

-   **Status Counts**: Shows the number of checkpoints currently in each
    > of the defined statuses:

    -   In Progress

    -   Ready for Grading

    -   Awaiting Student Review

    -   Student Review Received

    -   Completed

This helps teachers identify grading workload and get insights into
overall class performance.

# Tabs Overview

To access student responses, the teacher must click "More". A modal
window will open, showing three tabs, each represented by a clickable
circle:

-   General Tab

-   Question Tab

-   Mark Tab

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="1.3333333333333333in"}

The modal also includes:

-   A header with the checkpoint title

-   Two navigation buttons to go to the next or previous student

## General Tab

This tab contains information about the student\'s checkpoint
submission.![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="6.402777777777778in"}

**Structure:**

-   General Info

    -   Title

    -   Description

-   Challenge Info

    -   Time of the challenge

    -   Branch

-   Checkpoint Info

    -   Username

    -   Start time of the checkpoint

    -   Current status of the checkpoint

## Question Tab

Each question is displayed on a separate page, navigable using Next and
Previous buttons at the bottom

.![](data:image/png;base64,){width="2.1145833333333335in"
height="0.6041666666666666in"}

For all questions, each page contains:

-   Section Title and Description

> ![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
> height="2.5972222222222223in"}

-   Question Text

> ![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
> height="1.2083333333333333in"}

-   Student Answer

> ![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
> height="1.9305555555555556in"}

-   Explanation

> ![](data:image/png;base64,){width="5.09375in"
> height="2.09375in"}

-   Grade Field (auto-evaluated but editable)

    -   If the grade is changed manually, the original grade is shown
        > above as a reference.

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="0.9166666666666666in"}

-   Feedbacks (formatted as \[Time\]: \[Text\])

    -   Student Feedback

    -   Teacher Feedback

-   Comment Input (bottom-right field for teachers to write and submit
    > comments)

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="2.5972222222222223in"}

# Question Type-Specific Presentation:

-   Single Choice / Multiple Choice:

    -   Student answers shown as a list.

    -   Correct selections: Green

    -   Incorrect selections: Red

    -   Missed correct answers: Light Orange

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="3.1805555555555554in"}

-   Drag and Drop:

    -   The answer includes embedded questions with blank fields.

    -   Correct fill-ins: Green

    -   Incorrect fill-ins: Red, followed by an arrow and the correct
        > value.

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="1.8888888888888888in"}

-   Open Ended:

    -   Additional section: AI Explanation for the automatically
        > generated grade

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="1.9861111111111112in"}

## Grade Tab

The final tab summarizes the
grading.![](data:image/png;base64,){width="5.796875546806649in"
height="6.230195756780402in"}

## Content:

-   Grade Overview

    -   List of all questions and their assigned grades

-   Total Points

    -   Sum of all question scores

-   Final Mark

    -   Auto-computed based on grading

    -   If the total is a decimal, the rounded-up value is shown in a
        > separate field

    -   Clicking the arrow reveals an optional comment field for overall
        > feedback

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="2.5in"}

-   Submit Button

    -   Publishes the grade and teacher comments

    -   Changes the status of the evaluation (e.g., to "Awaiting Student
        > Review" or "Completed") in which the grade and question field
        > are not editable anymore

![](data:image/png;base64,){width="6.267716535433071in"
height="2.486111111111111in"}
